headline: Senate resolution to cancel an HHS rule on child care funding flexibility did not advance and did not take effect.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Department of Health and Human Services rule titled "Restoring Flexibility in the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF)." The CCDF is a federal program that gives money to states to help low-income families pay for child care. If adopted, the rule would have had no legal effect, and HHS could not have issued a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress. No official summary was available, so the rule's specific changes are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: State agencies that run child care assistance programs
who_it_affects.how: They would have been unable to use whatever added flexibility the HHS rule gave them in running CCDF programs.

who_it_affects.group: Low-income families who get help paying for child care through the CCDF
who_it_affects.how: The rules for their child care assistance would have stayed as they were before the HHS rule.

who_it_affects.group: Child care providers who accept CCDF subsidies
who_it_affects.how: The program rules that affect how they work with the subsidy program would not have included the changes in the HHS rule.
